other_exits: Historical signal scan: when both BuyPosOpen+BuyPosClose or SellPosOpen+SellPosClose are enabled and no direct close signal on SignalBar, the EA scans backward through bars to find the most recent opposite signal to determine close flags

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum controls sizing: LOT=fixed lots at MM value; FREEMARGIN/BALANCE/LOSSFREEMARGIN/LOSSBALANCE=fraction of margin/balance at MM percentage. MMMode input selects the mode.

custom_logic_notes: The EA uses a custom ADXCrossing indicator with two buffers: buffer 1 for up signals (non-zero and non-EMPTY_VALUE = buy signal) and buffer 0 for down signals (non-zero and non-EMPTY_VALUE = sell signal). Signal is read from SignalBar (default bar 1 = previous closed bar). When the EA has both open and close permissions for same direction, it performs a historical backward scan from SignalBar+1 to find the most recent opposing signal to set close flags. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose are input toggles that gate whether the EA is allowed to open or close long/short positions. Recount mechanism ensures signals are re-fetched if CopyBuffer fails. GlobalVariableDel_ is called on deinit for cleanup.
python_conversion_notes: The custom ADXCrossing indicator must be reimplemented or its logic reverse-engineered before Python conversion. It likely compares +DI and -DI lines of ADX for crossover signals. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, CIsNewBar, LoadHistory, and GlobalVariableDel_ functions that must all be reimplemented. The margin-based position sizing (4 modes) adds complexity. The historical backward signal scan for close determination when both open+close are enabled is an unusual pattern that must be carefully replicated. SL/TP are in points (not pips), and no 5-digit adjustment is present in the code itself—the TradeAlgorithms.mqh may handle it internally.
